title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — ἐφ' ᾧ πάντες ἥμαρτον; linger then flee to ἥμαρτον; Calvin French
pass_a_gloss: Next come eph' hoi pantes hemarton, which you treat as a stronghold. You pause on eph' hoi, then shift to hemarton. You will not wholly cast off the Churches' French Calvin rendering—because, or when, all sinned—even while you dislike it and lodge objections here and in chapter ix., which I will examine when I reach that chapter.
pass_b_english: Let us come to the following words, eph' hoi pantes hemarton. Here, forsooth, you think you have found a great defense of your cause. You linger a little on the words eph' hoi, presently, leaving them, you betake yourself to the word hemarton. Namely you were unwilling wholly to reject the version which our Churches use, although you openly enough show that it does not please you. And so, you say, let our French version stand and remain, which is John Calvin's, because, or when, all have sinned. Yet against it you cast some things in this chapter and in chapter ix., which, when I shall have come to that chapter, God helping, I will call back to examination.
source_text: Veniamus ad sequentes voces ἐφ' ᾧ πάντες ἥμαρτον. Hic magnum scilicet causae tuae putas te reperisse praesidium. In verbis ἐφ' ᾧ consistis paululum, mox iis desertis ad verbum ἥμαρτον te confers. Nempe tu versionem, qua utuntur Ecclesiae nostrae, noluisti prorsus reiicere, quamvis satis aperte prae te feras, eam tibi non probari. Itaque, inquis, stabiliatur & maneat versio nostra gallica, quae est Iohannis Calvini, eo quod, vel quando omnes peccaverunt. Adversus eam tamen nonnulla obicis hoc cap. & cap. ix. quae cum ad illud caput pervenero, Deo bene iuvante, ad examen revocabo.

choices.choice: Opponent treats ἐφ' ᾧ πάντες ἥμαρτον as stronghold but shifts from ἐφ' ᾧ to ἥμαρτον while keeping Calvin French
